docs.title: Fly: short FontLab imports
docs.text:
Fly gives scripts ten short names for the canonical FontLab scripting modules. Each alias returns the original module object. Importing fly alone loads none of its providers.

Documentation sources and local builds are available. Private-repository Pages publication is held by the owner on the current account plan; no public site is deployed.

from fly import fl, ap
import fly.ap.core.history.glyphs as history

Use Fly when writing scripts for FontLab. It keeps imports short while preserving the provider's module identity and import metadata. It supplies aliases; the target packages supply the APIs and FontLab supplies the native runtime.

Start with installation, then choose the correct import and provider. The development guide explains the host-free checks and their limits.

docs.title: Runtime boundaries
docs.text:
FontLab host work targets Python 3.11 on macOS arm64. Installing Fly in an external Python environment does not provide FontLab's native bindings or PythonQt. UI and active-font operations must follow the target package's host, thread and ownership requirements.

The ordinary import tests use stand-in providers. Historical native smoke results predate later shared-package refactors; current native acceptance remains open. A working documentation site does not establish native behavior.

docs.title: Development
docs.text: Fly's runtime is in src/fly; tests checks aliases, migration helpers and licence packaging. examples/native_smoke.py is a host smoke example. It requires FontLab and all providers; do not run it as a standalone native test.

docs.title: Host-free tests
docs.text:
After preparing the standalone environment, run from the checkout:

./test.sh -q -p no:cacheprovider

The script uses uv run --no-sync: pytest must already be installed. The packaging test builds an actual wheel and verifies the exact Apache licence, NOTICE and licensing metadata. Alias tests use stand-in modules, preserving the boundary between routing checks and real provider behavior.

Current native acceptance must check all ten aliases, both import forms, canonical metadata and child imports against the final artifacts. Active-font Feature workflows additionally need owned fonts and Apply/Undo/Redo/save/reopen proof. Those are separate from this website build.

docs.title: Build these pages
docs.text:
Build from the repository root in a separate Python 3.13 environment.

uv venv --python 3.13 .docs-venv
uv pip install --python .docs-venv/bin/python --require-hashes -r src_docs/requirements.txt
export PATH="$PWD/.docs-venv/bin:$PATH"
sh src_docs/build.sh
python -m unittest discover -s tests_docs -v

ProperDocs reads src_docs/mkdocs.yml and the Markdown in src_docs/md, then rebuilds docs/ in strict mode. The theme, fly-january 0.4.0 or later (remote theme assets), supplies the FontLab menu and footer. The menu labels this guide Fly. Search uses MaterialX's local index. src_docs/build.sh defaults SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH to the checkout's commit timestamp. CI captures the source commit's timestamp once and passes it to both builds; the generated commit's timestamp and later UTC dates do not change the output.

docs.title: Main-branch automation
docs.text:
Every push to main starts the repository's documentation workflow, including code-only changes. A first job builds and checks the source commit. If it is still current, it commits only changed generated docs and pushes normally. A stale run leaves current main untouched; a push failure is a failed run.

A dependent job checks out the resulting immutable commit, rebuilds the entire site, and requires byte-identical generated output. This second build also qualifies generated bot commits, whose token push does not recursively trigger another workflow. Unchanged output keeps the original commit and still gets the full verification. A passing build qualifies source and output, not deployment.

docs.title: Publication hold
docs.text:
Private-repository Pages publication is held by the owner: the current account plan does not support this private site, and no public site has been deployed. The workflow has no Pages write permission or automatic Pages request. Main-branch source work and generated-docs commits continue under that hold.

src_docs/request-pages.sh remains test-covered and dormant for qualified public reuse or future explicitly authorized publication. Do not invoke it or wire it into private delivery while the hold applies. Its local mocked tests remain part of the suite; they do not contact GitHub or establish a real deployment.

Any later authorized publication needs actual branch-source main:/docs settings, a qualified deployment SHA and live verification. The helper's Pages API builds the latest default branch and cannot atomically target an arbitrary SHA; existing head checks expose concurrent changes but cannot revoke a queued build.

docs.title: Imports and providers
docs.text:
Both from fly import ... and import fly.<alias> route to the original canonical module. Child imports use the same routing and preserve metadata, including native modules whose __spec__ is None.

Alias Canonical module Responsibility fl echopy.fontlab FontLab bindings fg echopy.fontgate FontGate bindings tr typerig TypeRig library pr echopy.fontpr FontLab command bridge qt PythonQt Host Qt binding ap fontlabapp Shared script and UI helpers qs pythonqtside PySide-style access to host PythonQt gp fontlab_glyport Glyphs.app compatibility fp fontlab_fontport fontParts/UFO interoperability pens fontlab_pens Pen and PointPen protocols

docs.title: Identity and child imports
docs.text:
from fly import gp, fp, pens
import fly.gp
import fly.fp
import fly.pens
import fontlab_glyport
import fontlab_fontport
import fontlab_pens

assert gp is fly.gp is fontlab_glyport
assert fp is fly.fp is fontlab_fontport
assert pens is fly.pens is fontlab_pens

Keep App's explicit domain paths when importing its submodules:

import fly.ap.core.history.glyphs as history
from fly.ap.fontui.feature_blocks import read_feature_blocks, write_feature_blocks
from fly.fp.pens import FontGatePointPen

Feature source helpers belong to App's fontui.feature_blocks. The shared fly.ap.core.scripting module also exposes lazy wrappers. General UI and shared script helpers belong in App; Fontport owns fontParts/UFO support and Glyport owns Glyphs.app compatibility.

docs.title: Pens
docs.text:
fly.pens exposes the complete canonical fontlab_pens module, including its public exports and submodules. App, Fontport and Glyport follow the same exact module routing; Fly does not select or wrap their APIs.

from fly import pens

recording = pens.RecordingPen()
transformed = pens.TransformPen(recording, (2, 0, 0, 3, 10, 20))
transformed.moveTo((1, 2))
transformed.lineTo((3, 4))
transformed.closePath()
assert recording.value[0] == ("moveTo", ((12, 26),))

Recording and transforms work outside FontLab. Native pens retain the provider's host requirements; Fly supplies no native emulation.

docs.title: Glyport's public API
docs.text:
from fly import gp

Glyphs = gp.GlyphsApp.Glyphs

gp.GlyphsApp is the lazy public fontlab_glyport.GlyphsApp module. First access to Glyphs binds a FontLab GUI-thread session. Outside FontLab, first bind an explicit backend with gp.GlyphsApp.use_backend(backend), then call gp.GlyphsApp.unbind() when finished. The backend must satisfy Glyport's contract; Fly does not supply one or broaden its compatibility guarantees.

docs.title: PythonQt and App
docs.text:
qt requires native PythonQt. Widgets are in QtGui; QObject is in PythonQt.private. Do not substitute a separate PySide runtime or construct another QApplication to exercise these imports.

Accessing ap alone does not construct App's Application or preference library. Native imports remain loaded in the host process, so a reused session is not a cold-import test.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Fly requires Python 3.11 or later. FontLab host work targets Python 3.11 arm64. Use the project checkout or an artifact supplied by its maintainer. This guide does not assume that current compatible provider releases are on PyPI.

docs.title: For a FontLab script
docs.text:
Install Fly and the required canonical providers into the same FontLab runtime using the maintainer's supported installation procedure. FontLab supplies PythonQt. Editable installations in FontLab are owner-managed; a standalone virtual environment is a separate runtime.

Current metadata declares these minimums:

Distribution Minimum fontlab-echopy 0.1.0 typerig 0.1.0 fontlab-fontlabapp 1.2.0 pythonqtside 0.1.0 fontlab-glyport 1.2.0 fontlab-fontport 1.2.0 fontlab-python-pens 1.0.0

Install fontlab-python-pens before Fly.

These are metadata minimums, not a guarantee that every newer script works with those versions. Meet each target package's own requirements. Install compatible providers from their reviewed checkouts or artifacts when released distributions are unavailable.

docs.title: Standalone development
docs.text:
Run these commands from your Fly checkout. They create a separate environment for Fly's host-free tests, without resolving or installing its providers:

uv venv --python cpython-3.11-macos-aarch64-none .venv
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python pytest
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python --no-deps -e .
./test.sh -q -p no:cacheprovider

This macOS arm64 recipe needs uv and a suitable Python, plus access to the pytest and build dependencies. It must not target FontLab's environment. See the repository README for the external scratch-directory recipe.

docs.title: Missing providers
docs.text: Accessing an alias imports its target. A missing target raises ModuleNotFoundError with alias context. An error caused by a missing internal dependency keeps its original error. Other provider exceptions propagate. Check that the required distribution is installed in the runtime actually executing your script; installing it in another virtual environment has no effect.

docs.title: Licence and attribution
docs.text:
Fly is licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0. The NOTICE credits the Echopy alias implementation. Both downloads are byte-identical to the repository's original attribution files.

The ten target modules retain their own licences. Fly's licence does not change their terms or grant rights to their implementation. This site describes public imports without embedding provider source.

The documentation uses ProperDocs, MaterialX and the fly-january 0.4.0 or later (remote theme assets). The theme's Apache 2.0 licence covers its CDN-hosted stylesheets and scripts. The generated MaterialX assets retain their bundled copyright notices.

docs.title: Current English browser payload
docs.text:
The browser-component record identifies the notices and upstream packages for fly-january 0.4.0 or later (remote theme assets) and MaterialX 10.1.8, including the MaterialX source maps.

The English-only omission manifest binds all 35 unused lunr-languages 1.20.0 helpers, including Wordcut and TinySegmenter. Before removing them, the build verifies the theme and search language, the search index, local HTML references and the hashes of all nine retained MaterialX assets. Of these, the theme rescales rem lengths in two stylesheets and leaves the other seven byte-identical.

The main source map retains 211 preferred sources, including 128 exact NPM source matches; the worker map retains 13 sources, including Lunr 2.3.9. The exact clipboard distribution embeds its dependencies; select, good-listener and delegate retain their upstream README MIT link and Zeno Rocha attribution, without invented standalone licence text or dates. CSS maps retain source names without embedded source bodies.

Material Design icons retain the Pictogrammers notice and Apache 2.0 icon terms or specifically stated underlying terms; code is MIT. Font Awesome Free retains Fonticons attribution and CC-BY 4.0 terms. Octicons retains GitHub's MIT notice; Lucide retains ISC and inherited notices. Of 45 observed ordered SVG path tuples, 43 match installed MaterialX icon path tuples exactly, including fontawesome/solid/caret-down.svg used by --md-version-icon. Its unchanged CSS header identifies Font Awesome Free 7.1.0, Copyright 2025 Fonticons, Inc., and CC-BY-4.0 icon terms; the full Font Awesome notice remains available below. The official Font Awesome 7.1.0 NPM caret SVG has different raw path bytes from the installed icon and CSS. The two unmatched Lucide focus/download tuples retain their pinned SCSS attribution. No unchanged-primary SVG, whole-geometry or optimizer-recipe equivalence is claimed.

The browser loads the FontLab menu and footer script from FontLab, fonts from Adobe and Google, and the PhotoSwipe 5.4.4 stylesheet from jsDelivr. The theme requests PhotoSwipe scripts on pages with lightbox links. These services supply their own responses. The site contains no font binaries.
